ops.statement: When a hook or decision depends on a harness-supplied payload field (e.g. a Stop-hook's `cwd`), verify the field's presence against the harness contract (docs), AND make the regression test drive the REAL writer path that populates it (here: run handle_post_tool_use to write the binding, then decide_stop), not a hand-injected fixture. A hand-set fixture asserts the field is present and passes green even if production never delivers it, hiding a silent no-op fix.
ops.grounding: .agent-work/stop-rail-151/plan-critic-disposition.md 'Finding 1' (cold critic: fix rode an unverified assumption that Stop carries cwd; injected-cwd unit tests would pass green even if prod lacks it) + verified via claude-code-guide official hooks docs; regression test (a) reshaped production-shaped in tests/test_spine_rail.py::test_stop_foreign_worktree_parent_not_blocked
ops.bank_reason: Single instance so far. A second run where a harness-field assumption is masked by injected fixtures would confirm this as a repo-wide testing pattern worth graduating into a testing-conventions doc (alongside test-harness-concurrency-failsafe), rather than a one-off caught by a critic.
